target.title: fix(feishu): route chat tools through contextual accounts
target.body:
﻿Related: #96657

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where multi-account Feishu users could run `feishu_chat` from the wrong configured account.

`feishu_chat` covers the `info`, `members`, and `member_info` actions. Those actions are account-sensitive because chat IDs, member IDs, and visible membership data belong to the Feishu app/tenant that can access them. Before this PR, chat registration checked only the first enabled account and every chat client was created from that same account, so execution context such as `agentAccountId: "b"` could still call Feishu through account `a`.

This caused two concrete failures:

- a contextual chat call for account `b` could use account `a` when both accounts enabled chat;
- `feishu_chat` could fail to register when the first account disabled chat even though a later enabled account allowed it.

This PR is intentionally narrower than #96657. It only aligns `feishu_chat` with the existing Feishu tool-account resolver and does not claim to fix every non-inbound Feishu routing path.

## Why This Change Was Made

`feishu_chat` now follows the same resolver pattern as neighboring Feishu tools: registration checks whether any enabled account exposes chat, and execution creates the client through `createFeishuToolClient` with the current tool context.

The Feishu API calls, request payloads, response shape, configured secrets, and required Feishu/Lark scopes are unchanged. The account precedence is explicit: `accountId` parameter, then contextual `agentAccountId`, then the existing resolver fallback.

## User Impact

Single-account Feishu setups keep the same behavior.

Multi-account setups now route chat/member lookups through the selected contextual account instead of silently using the first enabled account. If the selected contextual account has `tools.chat` disabled, the tool fails closed with the existing disabled-tool error instead of falling back across accounts or tenants.

## Evidence

Focused regression coverage verifies:

- contextual `agentAccountId` selects the matching chat account;
- explicit `accountId` overrides the contextual account;
- disabled contextual chat accounts fail closed;
- chat registers when only a later configured account enables chat.

Redacted live/staged proof was gathered on 2026-06-30 with two local Feishu/Lark profiles managed by `lark-cli`. Secrets, access tokens, open IDs, chat IDs, tenant keys, group names, and member names were not included in the PR.

```text
live provider check:
- profile a: bot identity ready, chat get returned expected chat fields
- profile b: bot/user identities ready, chat list/get returned expected chat fields

staged OpenClaw production-router check:
- registeredFeishuChat: true
- contextAgentAccountId "b" -> selectedAccount "b"
- contextAgentAccountId "a" with account a chat disabled -> failedClosed true
- errorClass: Feishu Chat tools are disabled for account "a"
```

Validation:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/feishu/src/chat.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/tool-account-routing.test.ts` - passed, 2 files / 32 tests
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test-local-feishu-chat-slim.tsbuildinfo` - passed
- `pnpm test:extension feishu` - passed, 73 files / 979 tests
- `git diff --check` - passed

AI-assisted: yes, prepared with Codex GPT-5.5 xhigh review assistance.
